_rationale: docs/QUALITY-CONTRACT.md. Notes below hold no measured status on purpose: for status run `python tools/gate/gate.py run --project .`

app._note: unused; kept in the shape the gate expects so a future served component has somewhere to go

build._note: the only subproject with an installable manifest; tools/ has none and imports stdlib only

unit.cmd: python -m pytest tests/ -q && python tools/gate/gate.py selftest && python tools/review/panel.py selftest && cd intent-control-plane && uv run pytest -q
unit._note: every automated-test entrypoint in the repo, including both oracles' own selftests
unit._timeout_note: Raised 300 -> 900 on 2026-07-31 with the measurement rather than by feel. The 300s budget was set when the root suite was 70 tests in about 47s. It is now 331 tests in 182s, and this domain chains FOUR commands: the root suite, the gate selftest, the panel selftest, and the intent-control-plane suite at about 50s. Total is roughly 250s on an idle machine and it timed out at 300s three times on 2026-07-31 under concurrent load, which produced a FAIL that named no failing test and sent two diagnoses down the wrong path. The honest alternative is splitting this into unit and subproject domains so a slow subproject cannot mask a fast regression; that is a contract shape change and is deferred to a ticket rather than done inside a timeout bump. Falsifier: if the suite passes 600s this number is hiding growth again and the split is overdue.

waived.reason: HOOKGATE-01, pre-existing and NOT caused by this branch. tests/test_hookgate.py compares tracked tools/hookgate/src/rules.rs against the live ~/.claude/hooks/safety_gate.py, and neither side is touched here; the live file was last written 2026-08-05, before this work started. 376 passed, 1 failed, 13 skipped. The fix named in the test's own error message, `python tools/hookgate/regen_rules.py`, is NOT applied on purpose, because it would relax a safety guard in the same command that turns the test green: committed rules.rs blocks --force(-with-lease)?|-f while the live safety_gate.py blocks --force(?!-with-lease) and permits force-with-lease. I ran the regen while diagnosing, read the diff, and reverted it. Whether the compiled binary should stop blocking force-with-lease is an operator decision about a safety oracle. CONFIRM BY RUNNING, do not trust this sentence: `python -m pytest tests/test_hookgate.py -q` should fail with exactly one assertion naming rules.rs, and `python tools/hookgate/regen_rules.py --check` should print the Run: line. If the failure is anything else, this waiver is FALSE and must be revoked. Short expiry on purpose: an operator decision should close it, not a renewal.

types.cmd: python -m compileall -q -x "\\.venv|venv" . && cd intent-control-plane && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy
types._note: compileall is the documented fallback where no root lint config exists; ruff and mypy are configured inside intent-control-plane

e2e.na_reason: claude-setup serves no application of its own. tools/e2e/flow.py and tools/browser/cdp.py drive other repositories' running UIs from whichever contract is being evaluated; every .html in this tree is a static export, not a route. See docs/QUALITY-CONTRACT.md.

a11y_ux.na_reason: Reads the e2e report at a stricter threshold, and there is no e2e report because there is no served app. If any part of this repo grows a UI, both this and e2e move to a real cmd rather than staying NA by default.

security._note: known blind spot is documented beside the patterns in gate.py, not here

docs._note: TODO.md is in the list because this repo describes changes there and in docs/analysis/, not in CHANGELOG.md

pipeline._note: local-green and CI-green have to be about the same checks

review._note: artifact is matched by commit sha, not by tree, so one written against a dirty tree stays current for that commit
review._waiver_history: A waiver until 2026-08-02 was REMOVED on 2026-08-06, expired, because the one thing it still excused has been done rather than waited out. Its own closing sentence asked for exactly this: 'Short expiry on purpose: committing the tree should clear it, not renew it.' What it waived was that the review domain refuses to certify a dirty tree, and that the dirty work was not the waiver author's to commit. That work is now committed. Evidence, and the waiver text said to confirm by running rather than to trust the sentence: `python tools/review/panel.py run --project .` reports VERDICT: PASS (0 high, 0 medium, 0 low) over 756 added lines across 12 files, and the artifact it wrote names commit e0d03bc3be4e with reviewer persona-panel/local, so it is neither a self-review nor a verdict against a parent commit. Removing rather than renewing, because a renewed waiver on a condition that has been met is a disabled check. Full text of the removed waiver: Replaces the 2026-08-12 waiver, whose stated reason was measurably WRONG and is recorded here rather than deleted. It said all 5 HIGHs were matches against comments and docstrings. Three were prose (an English 'Delete ... + their selftest' in two docs/prior-art JSON records and a print() of a delete result), and two were REAL shell=True code on lines this branch added and then deleted, reported against line numbers now occupied by the comment recording that deletion. Comments were never the mechanism. Both defects are now fixed in the oracle rather than waived: sql-concat requires SQL structure (FROM/INTO/SET) as well as a concatenation, and added_lines drops any line the tree no longer contains at the position it claims. tests/test_panel_sql_concat.py and tests/test_panel_stale_lines.py pin both, 20 cases; mutate.py --spec panel is 10 of 10 caught. The panel now returns 0 high. WHAT IS STILL WAIVED is only this: the review domain refuses to certify a dirty tree ('_note' above), and this tree carries uncommitted work that is not mine to commit. Nothing about the code is being excused. CONFIRM BY RUNNING, do not trust this sentence: python tools/review/panel.py run --project . -- expected 'VERDICT: PASS  (0 high'. If that reports any high finding, this waiver is FALSE and must be revoked. Short expiry on purpose: committing the tree should clear it, not renew it.

perf.na_reason: No performance budget is declared for claude-setup. Every budget-shaped string in the tree is either another project's historical Lighthouse evidence or code that reports p95 without enforcing a threshold. Nobody has set a number to measure against.

codemap._note: every tracked directory states a purpose, and docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md matches the tree

waived.reason: GATE-LOOP-01, structural, not a stale map. codemap records a file COUNT per directory and counts state/reviews, while the gate's review domain requires state/reviews/<HEAD sha>.json to name HEAD exactly, and the gate itself runs panel.py during the run, which writes that artifact. So the act of measuring review invalidates codemap within the same run, and committing the artifact moves HEAD so the artifact names the parent. Observed both ways across six commits on 2026-08-06. The sole remaining complaint is `different: state/reviews`; every other directory is clean at 422 dirs with 0 undocumented. gate.py already carries GATE_OUTPUTS = ('state/gate-runs.jsonl', 'state/reviews/') for its own dirty calculation, so the concept exists and codemap.py does not share it, and review_artifact already supports a ${FP} tree fingerprint instead of ${SHA}. Either closes it, both are oracle edits, and this branch is about skills and personas. CONFIRM BY RUNNING: `python tools/map/codemap.py check` should report ONLY state/reviews as different. If it names any other directory, this waiver is FALSE and must be revoked.

docmap._note: Every tracked markdown file has a derivable or declared lifecycle status, and docs/DOCMAP.md matches what the documents imply. Declared 2026-07-31, six days after the tool was written: docmap ran clean the whole time and NOTHING enforced it, which is the same shape as a hook that cannot fire. A hand edit to DOCMAP.md reads as drift and fails, exactly as CODEBASE-MAP.md does, because both are generated. The residue that cannot be derived lives in docs/doc-status.txt, currently 44 rows against a stated ceiling of 37; growth past that means the derivation rules are wrong rather than that the registry should grow.

prior_art._note: every component over 300 lines of Python carries an unexpired record naming what else could do its job
prior_art._waiver_history: A waiver until 2026-08-01 was added on 2026-07-31 and REMOVED the same day, unexpired, because the thing it excused was done rather than waited out. Its reason was correct when written: commit 8a4217b brought syndication-engine (549 lines), whatsapp-query (1120) and tools/intent (1016) fully into tracking with no prior-art records, and inventing three records to clear a red domain would have fabricated the evidence this domain exists to demand. All three now exist with 7, 8 and 7 fetched-and-cited alternatives and counterarguments that argue against keeping our version. Recorded here rather than deleted, because L-2026-07-31-a is a waiver renewed twice on a reason nobody executed, and the counter-practice worth keeping is that a waiver ends when its reason does.
